record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Qualitative structure of nonconstant steady states
record.original_question: Whenever spatially non-constant steady states exist for the nonlocal multispecies perception system ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − ∇·(u_i∇(Σ_j=1^n γ_ij u_j g,R)), what qualitative properties do those steady states have? For example, what kinds of segregation, aggregation, or other spatial structures can occur?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. What are the qualitative properties of these non-constant steady states, whenever they exist? The recent work [24] provides some interesting insights and techniques in this direction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth domain (or the torus, equipped with periodic boundary conditions). For $n \geq 2$ species with densities $u_i = u_i(x,t) \geq 0$, $i=1,\dots,n$, consider the nonlocal advection–diffusion system
$$\partial_t u_i = d_i \Delta u_i \;-\; \nabla\!\cdot\!\Bigl(u_i\, \nabla\Bigl[\sum_{j=1}^n \gamma_{ij}\, (u_j * g_R)\Bigr]\Bigr), \qquad x\in\Omega,\ t>0,$$
together with no-flux (or periodic) boundary conditions. Here $d_i>0$ are diffusion coefficients, $\Gamma=(\gamma_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is an interaction matrix encoding attraction ($\gamma_{ij}>0$) and repulsion ($\gamma_{ij}<0$) between species, and 
$$(u_j * g_R)(x) := \int_{\Omega} g_R(x-y)\, u_j(y)\, dy$$
is a nonlocal spatial averaging of $u_j$ using a fixed radially symmetric detection kernel $g_R$ of perceptual radius $R>0$ (for example, a normalized indicator of the ball $B_R(0)$). Spatially constant steady states $(u_1^*,\dots,u_n^*)$ exist for any prescribed total masses $\int_\Omega u_i\,dx = m_i$.

Problem. Suppose that, for some choice of parameters $(d_i,\gamma_{ij},R,m_i)$, there exist spatially non-constant steady states of the system. Determine the qualitative properties of these non-constant steady states. In particular:
(a) Characterize the possible spatial structures (e.g. segregation between species, co-aggregation, territory-like piecewise-constant patterns, spike or interface profiles, periodic patterns).
(b) Identify which sign patterns and magnitudes of $\Gamma$, and which relations between $d_i$ and $R$, force or preclude each type of structure.
(c) Describe regularity, symmetry, monotonicity, and support/overlap properties of components $u_i$ at such steady states, and quantify multi-stability (number and classification of stable non-constant equilibria).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as open in the originating survey. Subsequent work has obtained partial results: methods for detecting local minimum energy states of multispecies nonlocal advection–diffusion systems have been developed, showing that even for two species up to four classes of local minimum-energy states can coexist, with patterns ranging from territory-like segregation to narrow spike-type solutions, together with intra/inter-species aggregation and repulsion. A full qualitative classification of all non-constant steady states remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Detecting minimum energy states and multi-stability in nonlocal advection–diffusion models for interacting species
status_evidence.snippet: Methods determine the qualitative structure of local minimum energy states of a broad class of multi-species nonlocal advection–diffusion models... even with two species, multi-stability with up to four classes of local minimum energy states can emerge... spatial sorting via aggregation and repulsion both within and between species... a mixture of territory-like segregation as well as narrow spike-type solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial qualitative classification of non-constant steady states has been obtained for the multispecies nonlocal advection–diffusion system.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 3. What are the qualitative properties of these non-constant steady states, whenever they exist?
status_evidence.claim: The qualitative structure of non-constant steady states is explicitly stated as an open problem.
